processHint: Restriction enzymes cut, DNA ligase joins — together they build recombinant DNA.
learnMore: Cut → insert → join → transform → replicate: this is how scientists engineer bacteria to make useful proteins.
quizQuestion: What does a restriction enzyme do?
tipCut: Restriction enzymes act like molecular scissors — they cut DNA only at specific short sequences.
tipInsert: The same restriction enzyme is used to cut out the target gene, so its cut ends match the plasmid's.
tipJoin: DNA ligase acts like glue, sealing the gene into the plasmid to form recombinant DNA.
tipTransform: Bacteria can be tricked into taking up plasmids from their surroundings — this is called transformation.
tipReplicate: Every time the bacterium divides, it copies the recombinant plasmid too — mass-producing the gene product.
